newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 16.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 16.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
Plutonic Resources Ltd said on Tuesday the resource estimate at its Centenary deposit in Western Australia has doubled to 2.1 million ounces.
Philip Morris Inc's Australian unit chief executive Henry Goldberg said he expected a price war to erupt in Australia by June that would cost the sector A$100 million in earnings in calendar 1997.

Suncorp Metway Ltd said on Wednesday it would be safe from takeover activity following expected bank industry rationalisation in response to the Wallis financial system inquiry. "We believe we will be on the sidelines (of any activity) for several years because of the (Queensland state) government's 67 percent stake," chief executive Steve Jones told a Morgan Stockbroking Ltd breakfast meeting.

Leading Australian gold mining group Normandy Mining Ltd said on Wednesday that it achieved a nine-month net profit of A$83.4 million. The company also said net profit in the latest three months to March 31 was A$31.8 million. There were no comparative figures.

San Miguel Corp on Tuesday won shareholder approval for a controversial plan to merge its lucrative Coca-Cola bottling company with Australia's Coca-Cola Amatil. However, a government representative, which controls 48 percent of San Miguel, said he wanted a renegotiation of the deal, with more CCL shares, and more San Miguel representatives on the board.
Rupert Murdoch said on Tuesday his 25-year-old son Lachlan would take control of his company's sometimes troublesome Australian operations.
